worldcombat.skill.hornleech.summary: Strike with a horn and recover health based on the damage dealt.
The horns deal about %1$s contact damage; the target's defence, type and crits are applied on the hit.
It charges up to %1$s blocks at %2$s blocks per tick with a %3$s block tip radius.
For each target gored, %1$s of the damage actually dealt is restored to the user; no healing is gained while the user is already at full health.
worldcombat.skill.hornleech.gore.on: Goring charge: charges further and punches through one target into a second (up to two), but each blow is slightly weaker and each target siphons less, with a longer wind-up, recovery and cooldown.
worldcombat.skill.hornleech.gore.off: Single gore: siphons more and recovers quickly, good for sustain.
worldcombat.skill.hornleech.timing: Range %1$s blocks; wind-up %2$s s, recovery %3$s s, costing %4$s PP, cooldown %5$s s from commit.
worldcombat.skill.hornleech.growth.0: From level %1$s the gore power rises to %2$s.
worldcombat.skill.hornleech.growth.1: From level %1$s the gore power rises to %2$s and the drain share to %3$s.
worldcombat.skill.hornleech.use.0: Lower the head and turn a stretch of ground into a hit
worldcombat.skill.hornleech.use.1: Trade the hit for healing and keep going
worldcombat.skill.hornleech.use.2: Punch through two targets in one goring charge
worldcombat.skill.hornleech.preference.g: On: charge further and punch through one target into a second (up to two), but each blow is slightly weaker and each target siphons less, with a longer wind-up, recovery and cooldown - good for breaking a line. Off: one gore that siphons more and recovers quickly.
worldcombat.skill.hornleech.preference.a: Beyond this distance the user closes in first. Larger chases harder and overshoots more easily.
Below this health ratio the user prefers horn leech as sustain; higher starts leaning on it for healing sooner.
The charge runs straight along the aim, goring only non-allies and settling each target once; with the goring form it catches up to two targets, otherwise only one. It stops when terrain blocks it or the distance runs out, and catching no one is a whiff.
